```{r, knitr, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE,
                      fig.align="center", comment="#>")

pkgs=c("FLCore", "FLBRP", "FLRebuild", "icesdata", "spict", "ggplot2", "ggplotFL")
ok  =all(vapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly=TRUE))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval=ok)

## JABBA takes about two minutes; set to FALSE to skip
runJabba=requireNamespace("JABBA", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("rjags", quietly=TRUE)
```

# Introduction

Diagnostics for different assessment methods are usually produced by
method-specific code (e.g. `spict::plotspict.*`, `JABBA::jbplot_*`,
`ss3diags`), which makes it hard to compare methods and ties the plots to
package internals. Here, extraction is separated from plotting:

1. each assessment is converted to a common summary, a `cmpAssess`, holding
   * `ts`, an `FLQuants` of annual biomass (`stock`), `harvest`, `catch`,
     $B/B_{MSY}$ (`bbmsy`) and $F/F_{MSY}$ (`ffmsy`), with `lower` and
     `upper` `FLQuants` (or iters) for the uncertainty;
   * `refpts`, an `FLPar` with `bmsy`, `fmsy`, `msy`, `k`, `r` and `n`;
   * `index`, a data.frame of observations and fits (`series`, `year`,
     `obs`, `hat`, `lower`, `upper`), `resid` and `process` residuals
     (`series`, `year`, `residual`), the production function `curve`
     (`stock`, `yield`), and `prior`/posterior densities or draws;
   * `peels`, a named list of `cmpAssess` from retrospective fits;
2. the `cmp*` functions plot one assessment or a named list of them,
   coloured by method.

Mohn's rho, the hindcast and MASE, and the runs test are calculated from
the common summary, so no method-specific code is needed. The converters are
`flbrp2cmp` (an `FLStock` and `FLBRP`), `spict2cmp` (using only the exported
SPiCT API), `biodyn2cmp` and `jabba2cmp`.

North Sea plaice is used to compare

* the age-structured assessment (ICES) and its equilibrium reference points
  (`FLBRP`), using exploitable biomass and the harvest rate (catch/biomass);
* SPiCT and a `biodyn`, both fitted to catch and exploitable biomass, with
  priors / starting values from the `FLBRP`-derived Pella-Tomlinson
  parameters;
* JABBA, with priors from the `FLBRP` (`FLRebuild::runJABBA`).

```{r, pkgs}
library(FLCore)
library(FLBRP)
library(ggplotFL)
library(ggplot2)
library(spict)
library(mpb)
```

# Assessments

## Age-structured assessment and FLBRP

```{r, flbrp}
data(icesdata, package="icesdata")
stk=window(icesdata[["ple.27.420"]], end=2020)

eq =FLRebuild::eql(stk, model="bevholtSV")
rf =FLRebuild::refptsEB(eq)
pt =FLRebuild::pellatParams(FLPar(msy =rf["msy",   "yield"],
                                  bmsy=rf["msy",   "eb"],
                                  k   =rf["virgin","eb"]))
idx=FLRebuild::ebiomass(stk)
psi=c(idx[, 1])/c(pt["k"])

asFLBRP=flbrp2cmp(stk, eq, name="FLBRP", biomass="eb", harvest="hr")
asFLBRP
```

## SPiCT

```{r, spict}
cv2sd=function(x) sqrt(log(1+x^2))
scale=1000
yrs  =an(dimnames(catch(stk))$year)

inp=list(obsC=c(catch(stk))/scale, timeC=yrs,
         obsI=c(idx)/scale,        timeI=yrs,
         dteuler=1/4)
inp$priors=list(
  logr     =c(log(c(pt["r"])),       cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logK     =c(log(c(pt["k"])/scale), cv2sd(0.5), 1),
  logn     =c(log(c(pt["p"])+1),     cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logbkfrac=c(log(psi),              cv2sd(0.3), 1),
  logsdi   =c(log(0.1),              0.5,        1))
inp=check.inp(inp, verbose=FALSE)

fit=fit.spict(inp)
fit=calc.osa.resid(fit)
fit=calc.process.resid(fit)
fit=retro(fit, nretroyear=5)

asSPiCT=spict2cmp(fit, name="SPiCT", scale=scale, process="generic")
```

The process residuals are calculated from the production function for all
methods (`process="generic"`), so that they are comparable; the SPiCT
process residuals for B and F are used with `process="spict"`.

## biodyn

The `biodyn` starts from the `FLBRP`-derived Pella-Tomlinson parameters,
with the shape and initial depletion fixed. Retrospective peels are refitted
to truncated data, and each peel is projected one year with the observed
catch, so that it predicts the next index observation.

```{r, biodyn}
bd=biodyn(params=FLPar(r=c(pt["r"]), k=c(pt["k"]), p=c(pt["p"]), b0=psi),
          catch=catch(stk))
setParams( bd)=idx
setControl(bd)=params(bd)
control(bd)[c("p", "b0"), "phase"]=-1
bd=fit(bd, idx)

biodynPeel=function(bd, idx, end) {
  p  =fit(window(bd, end=end), window(idx, end=end))
  ext=window(p, end=end+1)
  catch(ext)[, ac(end+1)]=catch(bd)[, ac(end+1)]
  fwd(ext, catch=catch(ext)[, ac(end+1)])}

bdPeels=lapply(2019:2015, function(y) biodynPeel(bd, idx, y))

asBiodyn=biodyn2cmp(bd, name="biodyn", peels=bdPeels)
```

## JABBA

```{r, jabba, eval=ok&&runJabba}
jb=FLRebuild::runJABBA(stk, method="flbrp", quick=TRUE, nc=2)
asJABBA=jabba2cmp(jb, name="JABBA")
```

```{r, list}
asmt=list(FLBRP=asFLBRP, SPiCT=asSPiCT, biodyn=asBiodyn)
if (exists("asJABBA")) asmt$JABBA=asJABBA
names(asmt)
```

# Time series

```{r, ts, fig.height=6.5}
cmpTS(asmt)
```

```{r, status, fig.height=5}
cmpStatus(asmt)
```

Since `ts` is an `FLQuants`, ggplotFL can be used directly, e.g. to compare
$B/B_{MSY}$ across methods

```{r, ggplotfl, fig.height=3.5}
bb=FLQuants(lapply(asmt, function(x) x$ts$bbmsy))

ggplot(bb, aes(year, data, colour=qname)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype=2) +
  labs(x="Year", y=expression(B/B[MSY]), colour=NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

or plot a single method with `plot`

```{r, ggplotfl2, fig.height=5}
plot(asmt$biodyn$ts[c("stock", "harvest", "catch")])
```

# Kobe phase plot

```{r, kobe, fig.height=6}
cmpKobe(asmt)
```

# Production functions

The `FLBRP` curve is the equilibrium yield against equilibrium exploitable
biomass; for the biomass dynamic models it is the Pella-Tomlinson
production function. Points are the realised surplus production
$B_{t+1}-B_t+C_t$ of each method.

```{r, prod, fig.height=5.5}
cmpProduction(asmt)
```

# Fits to the data

```{r, fit, fig.height=6}
cmpFit(asmt)
```

# Residuals

Observation residuals (one-step-ahead for SPiCT, $\log(obs/hat)$
otherwise), with runs tests.

```{r, runs, fig.height=6}
cmpRuns(asmt)
```

```{r, acf, fig.height=4}
cmpACF(asmt)
```

```{r, qq, fig.height=4}
cmpQQ(asmt)
```

## Process residuals

$\log(B_{t+1}/(B_t+P(B_t)-C_t))$, where $P$ is each method's production
function. The `biodyn` is deterministic given its parameters and the catch,
so its process residuals are zero to numerical precision (a check on the
calculation); for the age-structured assessment they show how far its
biomass dynamics depart from the equilibrium yield curve.

```{r, process, fig.height=6}
cmpProcess(asmt)
```

```{r, processacf, fig.height=3}
cmpACF(asmt, "process")
```

# Retrospective analysis

Mohn's rho is calculated by `mohnsRho` from the peels, for methods that
have them.

```{r, retro, fig.height=5}
cmpRetro(asmt)
```

# Hindcast cross-validation

One-year-ahead predictions of the index from each peel, with the MASE
(`cmpMASE`) relative to a naive (last observation) prediction.

```{r, hindcast, fig.height=4}
cmpHindcast(asmt, series="Index 1")
```

```{r, hindcastdf}
hc=cmpHindcastDF(asmt)
do.call(rbind, lapply(split(hc, hc[, c("method", "series")], drop=TRUE), function(x)
  data.frame(method=x$method[1], series=x$series[1],
             MASE=cmpMASE(x$obs, x$pred, x$naive))))
```

# Priors and posteriors

Priors are dashed and posteriors solid. For SPiCT the posterior is the
normal approximation on the log scale; for JABBA it is the MCMC sample
(with `quick=TRUE`, so a bimodal posterior may indicate chains that have
not mixed).

```{r, priors, fig.height=5.5}
cmpPriors(asmt, parameters=c("r", "k", "n", "psi"))
```
